ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA_SIZE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Total size (in bytes) of the data to be transferred. The complete transfer operation may consist of multiple chunks of data as specified by the CHUNK_DATA_SIZE register.
Minimum: 1 byte. Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation. Works in conjunction with the TRANSFER_WIDTH register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA_SIZE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Size (in bytes) for a single DMA transfer. In hardware handshake mode, the DMA reads in chunks of CHUNK_DATA_SIZE from the peripheral. For a single memory transfer CHUNK_DATA_SIZE and TOTAL_DATA_SIZE are set to the same value.
Minimum: 1 byte. Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation. Works in conjunction with the TRANSFER_WIDTH register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TRANSACTION_WIDTH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Denotes the width of each transaction that the DMA shall issue during the data movement.
Multiple transactions of this width will be issued until TOTAL_DATA_SIZE bytes have been transferred. Note that firmware may need to set a different value if a receiving IP supports a read / write transaction width that is less than 1 DWORD. This does not affect the wrap-around mechanism. Note that the value 3 for this register represents an invalid configuration that leads to an error.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: KEY_SHARE0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Initial Key Registers Share 0.
The actual initial key corresponds to Initial Key Registers Share 0 XORed with Initial Key Registers Share 1. Loaded into the internal Full Key register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. All key registers (Share 0 and Share 1) must be written at least once when the key is changed, regardless of key length (write random data for unused bits). The order in which the registers are updated does not matter. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: KEY_SHARE1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Initial Key Registers Share 1.
The actual initial key corresponds to Initial Key Registers Share 0 XORed with Initial Key Registers Share 1. Loaded into the internal Full Key register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. All key registers (Share 0 and Share 1) must be written at least once when the key is changed, regardless of key length (write random data for unused bits). The order in which the registers are updated does not matter. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: IV
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Initialization Vector Registers.
The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode (see Control Register), respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA_IN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Input Data Registers.
If MANUAL_OPERATION=0 (see Control Register), the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption after all Input Data registers have been written. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. Loaded into the internal State register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. After that, the processor can update the Input Data registers (See INPUT_READY field of Status Register). Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA_OUT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Output Data Register.
Holds the output data produced by the AES unit during the last encryption/decryption operation. If MANUAL_OPERATION=0 (see Control Register), the AES unit is stalled when the previous output data has not yet been read and is about to be overwritten. Each register has to be read at least once. The order in which the registers are read does not matter. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: OPERATION
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MODE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b11_1111).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: KEY_LEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SIDELOAD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers KEY_SHARE1_0 - KEY_SHARE1_7 (0).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PRNG_RESEED_RATE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MANUAL_OPERATION
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode (0), the AES unit automatically i) starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and ii) stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. This is the most efficient mode to operate in. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode (1), the AES unit i) only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger (see Trigger Register), and ii) overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not. This mode is useful if software needs full control over the AES unit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FORCE_MASKS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share (KEY_SHARE1_0 - KEY_SHARE1_7) must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_AUX_REGWEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Auxiliary Control Register configuration enable bit. If this is cleared to 0, the Auxiliary Control Register cannot be written anymore.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: START
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Keep AES unit paused (0) or trigger the encryption/decryption of one data block (1). This trigger is cleared to `0` if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 or if MODE=AES_NONE (see Control Register).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Keep current values in Initial Key, internal Full Key and Decryption Key registers, IV registers and Input Data registers (0) or clear all those registers with pseudo-random data (1).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA_OUT_CLEAR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Keep current values in Output Data registers (0) or clear those registers with pseudo-random data (1).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PRNG_RESEED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Keep continuing with the current states of the internal pseudo-random number generators used for register clearing and masking (0) or perform a reseed of the internal states from the connected entropy source (1). If the KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED bit in the Auxiliary Control Register is set to one, this trigger will automatically get set after providing a new initial key.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: IDLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is `0` if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also `0` if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: STALL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1 (see Control Register).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: OUTPUT_LOST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to `1`, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 (see Control Register).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: OUTPUT_VALID
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INPUT_READY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is `0` (not ready).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ALERT_FATAL_FAULT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PHASE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 6-bit one-hot field to select the phase of the Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) of operation. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to GCM_INIT (6'b00_0001). In case support for GCM has been disabled at compile time, this field is not writable and always reads as GCM_INIT (6'b00_0001).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: NUM_VALID_BYTES
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Number of valid bytes of the current input block. Only the last block in the GCM_AAD and GCM_TEXT phases are expected to have not all bytes marked as valid. For all other blocks, the number of valid bytes should be set to 16. Invalid input values, i.e., the value 5'b0_0000, and all other values different from 5'b1_0000 in case GCM is not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to 5'b1_0000.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: hmac
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Accelerator for SHA-2 256/384/512-based keyed HMAC and the hash function

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hmac_done
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: HMAC/SHA-2 has completed.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The message FIFO is empty. This interrupt is raised only if the message FIFO is actually writable by software, i.e., if all of the following conditions are met: i) The HMAC block is not running in HMAC mode and performing the second round of computing the final hash of the outer key as well as the result of the first round using the inner key. ii) Software has not yet written the Process or Stop command to finish the hashing operation. For the interrupt to be raised, the message FIFO must also have been full previously. Otherwise, the hardware empties the FIFO faster than software can fill it and there is no point in interrupting the software to inform it about the message FIFO being empty.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hmac_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: HMAC error has occurred. ERR_CODE register shows which error occurred.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.hmac_done is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.fifo_empty is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.hmac_err is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.hmac_done to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.fifo_empty to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hmac_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.hmac_err to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fatal_fault
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hmac_en
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
HMAC datapath enable.
If this bit is 1, HMAC operates when `hash_start` toggles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sha_en
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
SHA-2 enable.
If 0, the SHA engine will not initiate compression, this is used to stop operation of the SHA-2 engine until configuration has been done. When the SHA-2 engine is disabled the digest is cleared.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: endian_swap
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Endian swap.
If 0, each value will be added to the message in little-endian byte order. The value is written to MSG_FIFO same to the SW writes. If 1, then each individual multi-byte value, regardless of its alignment, written to !!MSG_FIFO will be added to the message in big-endian byte order. A message written to !!MSG_FIFO one byte at a time will not be affected by this setting. From a hardware perspective byte swaps are performed on a TL-UL word granularity.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: digest_swap
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Digest register byte swap.
If 1 the value in each digest output register is converted to big-endian byte order. This setting does not affect the order of the digest output registers, !!DIGEST_0 still contains the first 4 bytes of the digest.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: key_swap
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Key register byte swap (deprecated: KEY path is for DV only; production uses key manager sideload).
If 1 the endianness of each KEY_* register is swapped. Default value (value 0) is big endian representation of the KEY_* CSRs.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: digest_size
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Digest size configuration.
This is a 4-bit one-hot encoded field to select digest size for either HMAC or SHA-2. Invalid/unsupported values, i.e., values that don't correspond to SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512, are mapped to SHA2_None.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: key_length
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Key length configuration.
This is a 6-bit one-hot encoded field to configure the key length for HMAC.
The HMAC can be programmed with the following key lengths: 128-bit, 256-bit, 384-bit, 512-bit and 1024-bit. But the HMAC supports any arbitrary key length: the software should configure the HMAC with the next largest supported key length and concatenate zeros to reach the programmed key length. The position of these zeros depends on the endianness, thus on the programmed [`CFG.key_swap`](registers.md#cfg--key_swap). For example, for an 80-bit key, HMAC should be configured with an 128-bit key length, fed with the 80-bit key and with 48 zero-bits.
Note that the key length cannot be greater than the block size: up to 1024-bit for SHA-2 384/512 and up to 512-bit for SHA-2 256. The value of this register is irrelevant when only SHA-2 (not keyed HMAC) is configured. However, for HMAC mode (`hmac_en == 1`), when HMAC is triggered to start while !!KEY_LENGTH holds `Key_None` or !!KEY_LENGTH holds `Key_1024` for !!DIGEST_SIZE = `SHA2_256`, starting is blocked and an error is signalled to SW.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hash_start
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If 1 is written into this field, SHA-2 or HMAC begins its operation. CPU must configure relative information first, such as the digest size, secret key and the key length.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hash_process
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If 1 is written to this field, SHA-2 or HMAC calculates the digest or signing based on currently received message.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hash_stop
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When 1 is written to this field, SHA-2 or HMAC will afterwards set the `hmac_done` interrupt as soon as the current block has been hashed. The hash can then be read from the registers !!DIGEST_0 to !!DIGEST_15. Together with the message length in !!MSG_LENGTH_LOWER and !!MSG_LENGTH_UPPER, this forms the information that has to be saved before switching context.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hash_continue
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When 1 is written to this field, SHA-2 or HMAC will continue hashing based on the current hash in the digest registers and the message length, which both have to be restored to switch context.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hmac_idle
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: HMAC idle status. When IDLE, the `DIGEST` and the `MSG_LENGTH_LOWER`/`MSG_LENGTH_UPPER` can be written to from SW which enables restoring context (to support context switching).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO empty

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO full. Data written to the FIFO whilst it is full will cause back-pressure on the interconnect

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_depth
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO entry count.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: err_code
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If an error interrupt occurs, this register has information of error cause. Please take a look at `hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_sha2_pkg.sv:err_code_e enum type.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: KMAC/SHA3 absorbing has been completed

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The message FIFO is empty. This interrupt is raised only if the message FIFO is actually writable by software, i.e., if all of the following conditions are met: i) The KMAC block is not exercised by a hardware application interface. ii) The SHA3 block is in the Absorb state. iii) Software has not yet written the Process command to finish the absorption process. For the interrupt to be raised, the message FIFO must also have been full previously. Otherwise, the hardware empties the FIFO faster than software can fill it and there is no point in interrupting the software to inform it about the message FIFO being empty.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: kmac_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: KMAC/SHA3 error occurred. ERR_CODE register shows the details

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Configuration enable.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: kmac_en
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
KMAC datapath enable.
If this bit is 1, the incoming message is processed in KMAC with the secret key.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: kstrength
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Hashing Strength
3 bit field to select the security strength of SHA3 hashing engine. If mode field is set to SHAKE or cSHAKE, only 128 and 256 strength can be selected. Other value will result error when hashing starts.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: mode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Keccak hashing mode.
This module supports SHA3 main hashing algorithm and the part of its derived functions, SHAKE and cSHAKE with limitations. This field is to select the mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: msg_endianness
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Message Endianness.
If 1 then each individual multi-byte value, regardless of its alignment, written to !!MSG_FIFO will be added to the message in big-endian byte order. If 0, each value will be added to the message in little-endian byte order. A message written to !!MSG_FIFO one byte at a time will not be affected by this setting. From a hardware perspective byte swaps are performed on a TL-UL word granularity.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: state_endianness
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
State Endianness.
If 1 then each individual word in the !!STATE output register is converted to big-endian byte order. The order of the words in relation to one another is not changed. This setting does not affect how the state is interpreted during computation.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sideload
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Sideloaded Key. Deprecated: defaults to 1 (sideload). Set to 0 for DV testing with SW key path only.
If 1, KMAC uses KeyMgr sideloaded key for SW initiated KMAC operation. KMAC uses the sideloaded key regardless of this configuration when KeyMgr initiates the KMAC operation for Key Derivation Function (KDF).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: entropy_mode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Entropy Mode
Using this field, software can configure mode of operation of the internal pseudo-random number generator (PRNG).
Note that once software has configured a value different from `idle_mode` after reset, and set the !!CFG_SHADOWED.entropy_ready bit afterwards, the PRNG configuration cannot be changed anymore (unless an EDN request timeout occurs when running in EDN mode). Further writes to this field will change the value received upon reading the register, but they will be ignored by the internal hardware.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: entropy_fast_process
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Entropy Fast process mode.
If 1, entropy logic uses garbage data while not processing the KMAC key block. It will re-use previous entropy value and will not expand the entropy when it is consumed. Only it refreshes the entropy while processing the secret key block. This process should not be used if SCA resistance is required because it may cause side channel leakage.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: msg_mask
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Message Masking with PRNG.
If 1, KMAC applies PRNG to the input messages to the Keccak module when KMAC mode is on.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: entropy_ready
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Entropy Ready status.
Software sets this field to allow the entropy generator in KMAC to fetch the entropy and run.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: en_unsupported_modestrength
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Enable Unsupported Mode and Strength configs.
SW may set this field for KMAC to move forward with unsupported Keccak Mode and Strength configurations, such as cSHAKE512.
If not set, KMAC won't propagate the SW command (CmdStart) to the rest of the blocks (AppIntf, KMAC Core, SHA3).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: cmd
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Issue a command to the KMAC/SHA3 IP. The command is sparse encoded. To prevent sw from writing multiple commands at once, the field is defined as enum.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: entropy_req
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Software can set this bit to 1 to manually trigger the reseeding of the internal PRNG when running in EDN mode. This will also clear !!ENTROPY_REFRESH_HASH_CNT.
Note that the hardware may miss the trigger pulse if the module is not idle, or if the module is currently performing a reseed operation.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hash_cnt_clr
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Software can set this bit to 1 to manually clear !!ENTROPY_REFRESH_HASH_CNT.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: err_processed
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When error occurs and one of the state machine stays at Error handling state, SW may process the error based on ERR_CODE, then let FSM back to the reset state

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sha3_idle
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If 1, SHA3 hashing engine is in idle state.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sha3_absorb
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If 1, SHA3 is receiving message stream and processing it

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sha3_squeeze
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If 1, SHA3 completes sponge absorbing stage. In this stage, SW can manually run the hashing engine.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_depth
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Count of occupied entries in the message FIFO.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Message FIFO Empty indicator.
The FIFO's `Pass` parameter is set to `1'b 1`. So, by default, if the SHA engine is ready, the write data to FIFO just passes through.
In this case, `fifo_depth` remains **0**. `fifo_empty`, however, lowers the value to **0** for a cycle, then goes back to the empty state, **1**.
See the "Message FIFO" section in the spec for the reason.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fifo_full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Message FIFO Full indicator

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ALERT_FATAL_FAULT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No fatal fault has occurred inside the KMAC unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the KMAC unit needs to be reset (1), Examples for such faults include i) TL-UL bus integrity fault ii) storage errors in the shadow registers iii) errors in the message, round, or key counter iv) any internal FSM entering an invalid state v) an error in the redundant lfsr

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. KMAC operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: prescaler
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
EDN Wait timer prescaler.
EDN Wait timer has 16 bit value. The timer value is increased when the timer pulse is generated. Timer pulse is raises when the number of the clock cycles hit this prescaler value.
The exact period of the timer pulse is unknown as the KMAC input clock may contain jitters.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wait_timer
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
EDN request wait timer.
The entropy module in KMAC waits up to this field in the timer pulse after it sends request to EDN module. If the timer expires, the entropy module moves to an error state and notifies to the system.
If there is a pending EDN request during wait timer update, then this update is delayed until the EDN request is complete.
If 0, the entropy module waits the EDN response always. If EDN does not respond in this configuration, the software shall reset the IP.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force cs_cmd_req_done to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CS_ENTROPY_REQ
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force cs_entropy_req to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CS_HW_INST_EXC
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force cs_hw_inst_exc to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CS_FATAL_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force cs_fatal_err to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RECOV_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FATAL_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: REGWEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When true, all writeable registers can be modified. When false, they become read-only.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True will enable the CSRNG module. The modules of the entropy complex may only be enabled and disabled in a specific order, see Programmers Guide for details.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SW_APP_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True will enable reading from the !!GENBITS register. This application interface for software (register based) will be enabled only if the otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read input vector is set to the enable encoding.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: READ_INT_STATE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True will enable reading from the !!INT_STATE_VAL register. Reading the internal state of the enable instances will be enabled only if the otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read input vector is set to the enable encoding. Also, the !!INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE bit of the selected instance needs to be set to true for this to work.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIPS_FORCE_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True enables forcing the FIPS/CC compliance flag to true via the !!FIPS_FORCE register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: acmd
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Application Command: Selects one of five operations to perform. The commands supported are instantiate, reseed, generate, update, and uninstantiate. Each application interface port used by peripheral hardware commands a unique instance number in CSRNG.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: clen
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Command Length: Number of 32-bit words that can optionally be appended to the command. A value of zero will only transfer the command header. A value of 4'hc will transfer the header plus an additional twelve 32-bit words of data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: flag0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Command Flag0: flag0 is associated with current command. Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True will enable flag0 to be enabled. Note that flag0 is used for the instantiate and reseed commands only, for all other commands its value is ignored.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: glen
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Generate Length: Only defined for the generate command, this field is the total number of cryptographic entropy blocks requested. Each unit represents 128 bits of entropy returned. The NIST reference name is max_number_of_bit_per_request, and this field size supports the maximum size of 219 bits. For the maximum size, this field should be set to 4096, resulting in a max_number_of_bit_per_request value of 4096 x 128 bits. For a smaller example, a value of 8 would return a total of 1024 bits.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESEED_INTERVAL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field will set the number of generate requests that can be made to CSRNG before a reseed request needs to be made. This register supports a maximum of 2^32 requests between reseeds. This register will be compared to a counter, which counts the number of generate commands between reseed or instantiate commands. If the counter reaches the value of this register, the violating command will be acknowledged with a status error. If the violating command was issued by a HW instance, an interrupt will be triggered.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESEED_COUNTER_0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reseed Counter indicating the number of completed Generate requests since the last Instantiate or Reseed command.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESEED_COUNTER_0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reseed Counter indicating the number of completed Generate requests since the last Instantiate or Reseed command.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESEED_COUNTER_0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reseed Counter indicating the number of completed Generate requests since the last Instantiate or Reseed command.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_RDY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit indicates when the command interface is ready to accept commands. Before starting to write a new command to !!SW_CMD_REQ, this field needs to be polled. 0b0: CSRNG is not ready to accept commands or the last command hasn't been acked yet. 0b1: CSRNG is ready to accept the next command.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_ACK
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This one bit field indicates when a SW command has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. It is set to low each time a new command is written to !!CMD_REQ. The field is set to high once a SW command request has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. 0b0: The last SW command has not been acknowledged yet. 0b1: The last SW command has been acknowledged.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This field represents the status code returned with the application command ack. It is updated each time a command ack is asserted on the internal application interface for software use. To check whether a command was successful, wait for !!INTR_STATE.CS_CMD_REQ_DONE or !!SW_CMD_STS.CMD_ACK to be high and then check the value of this field.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: GENBITS_VLD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when genbits are available on this application interface.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: GENBITS_FIPS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when genbits are FIPS/CC compliant.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: GENBITS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reading this register will get the generated bits that were requested with the generate request. This register must be read four times for each request made. For example, an application command generate request with a `clen` value of 4 requires this register to be read 16 times to get all of the data out of the FIFO path. Note that for !!GENBITS to be able to deliver random numbers, also !!CTRL.SW_APP_ENABLE needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool4True`. In addition, the otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read input needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool8True`. Otherwise, the register reads as 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Per-instance internal state read enable. Defines whether the internal state of the corresponding instance is readable via !!INT_STATE_VAL. Note that for !!INT_STATE_VAL to provide read access to the internal state, also !!CTRL.READ_INT_STATE needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool4True`. In addition, the otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read input needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool8True`.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE_REGWEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE register configuration enable bit. If this is cleared to 0, the INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE register cannot be written anymore.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INT_STATE_NUM
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field will set the number for which internal state can be selected for a read access. Up to 16 internal state values can be chosen from this register. The actual number of valid internal state fields is set by parameter NHwApps plus 1 software app. For those selections that point to reserved locations (greater than NHwApps plus 1), the returned value will be zero. Writing this register will also reset the internal read pointer for the !!INT_STATE_VAL register. Note: This register should be read back after being written to ensure that the !!INT_STATE_VAL read back is accurate.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INT_STATE_VAL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reading this register will dump out the contents of the selected internal state field. Since the internal state field is 448 bits wide, it will require 14 reads from this register to gather the entire field. Once 14 reads have been done, the internal read pointer (selects 32 bits of the 448 bit field) will reset to zero. The !!INT_STATE_NUM can be re-written at this time (internal read pointer is also reset), and then another internal state field can be read. Note that for !!INT_STATE_VAL to provide read access to the internal state, also !!CTRL.READ_INT_STATE needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool4True`. In addition, the otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read input needs to be set to `kMultiBitBool8True`. Also, the !!INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE bit of the selected instance needs to be set to true for this to work. Otherwise, the register reads as 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIPS_FORCE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Force the FIPS/CC compliance flag of individual instances to true. This allows CSRNG to set the output FIPS/CC compliance flag to true despite running in fully deterministic mode (flag0 being true). This can be useful e.g. for known-answer testing through entropy consumers accepting FIPS/CC compliant entropy only, or when firmware is used to derive FIPS/CC compliant entropy seeds. After setting a particular bit to 1, the FIPS/CC compliance flag of the corresponding instance will be forced to true upon the next Instantiate or Reseed command.
Note that for this to work, !!CTRL.FIPS_FORCE_ENABLE needs to be set to kMultiBitBool4True.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HW_EXC_STS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reading this register indicates whether one of the CSRNG HW instances has encountered an exception. Each bit corresponds to a particular hardware instance, with bit 0 corresponding to instance HW0, bit 1 corresponding to instance HW1, and so forth. (To monitor the status of requests made to the SW instance, check the !!SW_CMD_STS register). Writing a zero to this register resets the status bits.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ENABLE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the ENABLE field in the !!CTRL register is set to a value other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SW_APP_ENABLE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the SW_APP_ENABLE field in the !!CTRL register is set to a value other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: READ_INT_STATE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the READ_INT_STATE field in the !!CTRL register is set to a value other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIPS_FORCE_ENABLE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the FIPS_FORCE_ENABLE field in the !!CTRL register is set to a value other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ACMD_FLAG0_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the FLAG0 field in the Application Command is set to a value other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CS_BUS_CMP_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the software application port genbits bus value is equal to the prior valid value on the bus, indicating a possible attack. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STAGE_INVALID_ACMD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when an unsupported/illegal CSRNG command is received by the main state machine. The invalid command is ignored and CSRNG continues to operate. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STAGE_INVALID_CMD_SEQ_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when an out of order command is received by the main state machine. This happens when an instantiate command is sent for a state that was already instantiated or when any command other than instantiate is sent for a state that wasn't instantiated yet. The invalid command is ignored and CSRNG continues to operate. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STAGE_RESEED_CNT_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the maximum number of generate requests between reseeds is exceeded. The invalid generate command is ignored and CSRNG continues to operate. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SFIFO_CMD_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an error has been detected for the command stage command FIFO. The type of error is reflected in the type status bits (bits 28 through 30 of this register). This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SFIFO_GENBITS_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an error has been detected for the command stage genbits FIFO. The type of error is reflected in the type status bits (bits 28 through 30 of this register). This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STAGE_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an illegal state has been detected for the command stage state machine. This error will signal a fatal alert, and also an interrupt if enabled. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MAIN_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an illegal state has been detected for the main state machine. This error will signal a fatal alert, and also an interrupt if enabled. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTR_DRBG_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an illegal state has been detected for the ctr_drbg gen state machine. This error will signal a fatal alert, and also an interrupt if enabled. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AES_CIPHER_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an AES fatal error has been detected. This error will signal a fatal alert, and also an interrupt if enabled. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTR_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when a mismatch in any of the hardened counters has been detected. This error will signal a fatal alert, and also an interrupt if enabled. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_WRITE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 15 of this this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any full FIFO that has been recieved a write pulse. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_READ_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 15 of this this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any empty FIFO that has recieved a read pulse. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_STATE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 15 of this this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any FIFO where both the empty and full status bits are set. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ERR_CODE_TEST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field will set the bit number for which an error will be forced in the hardware. This bit number is that same one found in the !!ERR_CODE register. The action of writing this register will force an error pulse. The sole purpose of this register is to test that any error properly propagates to either an interrupt or an alert.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MAIN_SM_STATE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This is the state of the CSRNG main state machine. See the RTL file `csrng_main_sm` for the meaning of the values.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: edn
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Distributes random numbers produced by CSRNG to hardware blocks

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_cmd_req_done
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Asserted when a software CSRNG request has completed.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_fatal_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Asserted when a FIFO error occurs.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_cmd_req_done
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.edn_cmd_req_done is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_fatal_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.edn_fatal_err is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_cmd_req_done
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.edn_cmd_req_done to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: edn_fatal_err
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.edn_fatal_err to 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: recov_alert
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fatal_alert
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: REGWEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When true, the CTRL can be written by software. When false, this field read-only. Defaults true, write zero to clear. Note that this needs to be cleared after initial configuration at boot in order to lock in the listed register settings.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True enables the EDN module. The modules of the entropy complex may only be enabled and disabled in a specific order, see Programmers Guide for details.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BOOT_REQ_MODE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True enables the boot-time request mode. In this mode, EDN automatically sends a boot-time request to the CSRNG application interface. The purpose of this mode is to request entropy as fast as possible after reset, and during chip boot time.
Note that this takes precedence over the AUTO_REQ_MODE field: If both fields are set, EDN enters boot-time request mode. If none of the fields are set, EDN enters Software Port Mode upon enabling.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTO_REQ_MODE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True enables auto request mode. In this mode, EDN automatically sends `generate` and `reseed` command requests to the CSRNG application interface. The purpose of this mode is to continuously deliver entropy to endpoints without firmware intervention.
For this to work, firmware has to 1) configure the !!GENERATE_CMD, !!RESEED_CMD, and !!MAX_NUM_REQS_BETWEEN_RESEEDS registers, and 2) to issue the first `instantiate` command via the !!SW_CMD_REQ register. Once this command has been acknowledged by CSRNG, the first `generate` command is sent out automatically, and a `reseed` command is sent after every MAX_NUM_REQS_BETWEEN_RESEEDS number of `generate` commands.
Note that the BOOT_REQ_MODE field takes precedence over this field: If both fields are set, EDN enters boot-time request mode. If none of the fields are set, EDN enters Software Port Mode upon enabling.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_FIFO_RST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field to kMultiBitBool4True clears the two command FIFOs: the RESEED_CMD FIFO and the GENERATE_CMD FIFO. This field must be set to the reset state by software before any further commands can be issued to these FIFOs.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BOOT_INS_CMD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
This field is used as the value for the `instantiate` command at boot time.
See [Command Header](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#command-header) for the meaning of the individual bits. Note that the hardware only supports a value of 0 for the `clen` field. If `clen` has a different value, EDN will hang. Fixing this requires disabling and restarting both EDN and CSRNG.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BOOT_GEN_CMD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
This field is used as the value for the `generate` command at boot time.
See [Command Header](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#command-header) for the meaning of the individual bits. Note that the hardware only supports a value of 0 for the `clen` field. If `clen` has a different value, EDN will hang. Fixing this requires disabling and restarting both EDN and CSRNG.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SW_CMD_REQ
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Any CSRNG action can be initiated by writing a CSRNG command to this register. Before any write operation to this register, firmware must read !!SW_CMD_STS to check whether EDN is ready to receive a new command or the next word of a previously started command.
While !!CTRL.AUTO_REQ_MODE is set, only the first instantiate command has any effect. After that command has been processed, writes to this register will have no effect on operation, until !!CTRL.AUTO_REQ_MODE is de-asserted and the state machine of EDN enters the `SwPortMode` state.
Refer to the [CSRNG documentation](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#general-command-format) for details on the command format.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_REG_RDY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit indicates when !!SW_CMD_REQ is ready to accept the next word. This bit has to be polled before each word of a command is written to !!SW_CMD_REQ. 0b0: The EDN is not ready to accept the next word yet. 0b1: The EDN is ready to accept the next word.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_RDY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit indicates when the EDN is ready to accept the next command. Before starting to write a new command to !!SW_CMD_REQ, this field needs to be polled. 0b0: The EDN is not ready to accept commands or the last command hasn't been acked yet. 0b1: The EDN is ready to accept the next command.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_ACK
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This one bit field indicates when a SW command has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. It is set to low each time a new command is written to !!SW_CMD_REQ. The field is set to high once a SW command request has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. 0b0: The last SW command has not been acknowledged yet. 0b1: The last SW command has been acknowledged.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This field represents the status code returned with the CSRNG application command ack. It is updated each time a SW command is acknowledged by CSRNG. To check whether a command was successful, wait for !!INTR_STATE.EDN_CMD_REQ_DONE or !!SW_CMD_STS.CMD_ACK to be high and then check the value of this field. A description of the command status types can be found [here](../../csrng/doc/registers.md#sw_cmd_sts--cmd_sts).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BOOT_MODE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This one bit field indicates whether the EDN is in the hardware controlled boot mode. 0b0: The EDN is not in boot mode. 0b1: The EDN is in boot mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTO_MODE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This one bit field indicates whether the EDN is in the hardware controlled part of auto mode. The instantiate command is issued via SW interface and is thus not part of the hardware controlled part of auto mode. 0b0: The EDN is not in the hardware controlled part of auto mode. 0b1: The EDN is in the hardware controlled part of auto mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_TYPE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This field contains the application command type of the hardware controlled command issued last. The application command selects one of five operations to perform. A description of the application command types can be found [here](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#command-description).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_ACK
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This one bit field indicates when a HW command has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. It is set to low each time a new command is sent to the CSRNG. The field is set to high once a HW command request has been acknowledged by the CSRNG. 0b0: The last HW command has not been acknowledged yet. 0b1: The last HW command has been acknowledged.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_STS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This field represents the status code returned with the CSRNG application command ack. It is updated each time a HW command is acknowledged by CSRNG. A description of the command status types can be found [here](../../csrng/doc/registers.md#sw_cmd_sts--cmd_sts).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESEED_CMD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Writing this register will fill a FIFO with up to 13 command words (32b words). When running in auto request mode, this FIFO is used to automatically send out a `reseed` command to the CSRNG application interface after every MAX_NUM_REQS_BETWEEN_RESEEDS number of `generate` commands.
See [General Command Format](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#general-command-format) for details about the command format.
Note that the number of additional data words provided must match the value of the `clen` field of the first word. Otherwise, undefined behavior may result. If more than 13 entries are written to the FIFO, they are ignored and EDN signals an `edn_fatal_err` interrupt as well as a fatal alert.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: GENERATE_CMD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Writing this register will fill a FIFO with up to 13 command words (32b words). When running auto request mode, this FIFO is used to automatically send out `generate` commands to the CSRNG application interface.
See [General Command Format](../../csrng/doc/theory_of_operation.md#general-command-format) for details about the command format.
Note that the number of additional data words provided must match the value of the `clen` field of the first word. Otherwise, undefined behavior may result. If more than 13 entries are written to the FIFO, they are ignored and EDN signals an `edn_fatal_err` interrupt as well as a fatal alert.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MAX_NUM_REQS_BETWEEN_RESEEDS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Setting this field will set the number of `generate` command requests that are made to CSRNG before a reseed request is made. This value only has meaning when running in auto request mode. This register supports a maximum of 2^32 `generate` requests between reseeds. This register will be used by a counter that counts down, triggering an automatic `reseed` request when it reaches zero.
Note that this value must be chosen smaller than or equal to the value configured in the [`RESEED_INTERVAL` register of CSRNG](../../csrng/doc/registers.md#reseed-interval).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_ENABLE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the EDN_ENABLE field is set to an illegal value, something other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BOOT_REQ_MODE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the BOOT_REQ_MODE field is set to an illegal value, something other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTO_REQ_MODE_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the !!CTRL.AUTO_REQ_MODE field is set to an illegal value, something other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CMD_FIFO_RST_FIELD_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the CMD_FIFO_RST field is set to an illegal value, something other than kMultiBitBool4True or kMultiBitBool4False. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_BUS_CMP_ALERT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the interal entropy bus value is equal to the prior valid value on the bus, indicating a possible attack. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CSRNG_ACK_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit is set when the CSRNG returns an acknowledgement where the status signal is non-zero. Writing a zero resets this status bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SFIFO_RESCMD_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an error has been detected for the reseed command FIFO. The type of error is reflected in the type status bits (bits 28 through 30 of this register). When this bit is set, a fatal error condition will result.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SFIFO_GENCMD_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an error has been detected for the generate command FIFO. The type of error is reflected in the type status bits (bits 28 through 30 of this register). When this bit is set, a fatal error condition will result. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_ACK_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an illegal state has been detected for the EDN ack stage state machine. This error will signal a fatal alert. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_MAIN_SM_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when an illegal state has been detected for the EDN main stage state machine. This error will signal a fatal alert. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EDN_CNTR_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when a hardened counter has detected an error condition. This error will signal a fatal alert. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_WRITE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 1 of this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any full FIFO that has received a write pulse. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_READ_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 1 of this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any empty FIFO that has received a read pulse. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_STATE_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This bit will be set to one when any of the source bits (bits 0 through 1 of this register) are asserted as a result of an error pulse generated from any FIFO where both the empty and full status bits are set or in case of error conditions inside the hardened counters. This bit will stay set until the next reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ERR_CODE_TEST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Setting this field will set the bit number for which an error will be forced in the hardware. This bit number is that same one found in the !!ERR_CODE register. The action of writing this register will force an error pulse. The sole purpose of this register is to test that any error properly propagates to either an interrupt or an alert.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MAIN_SM_STATE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: This is the state of the EDN main state machine. See the RTL file `edn_main_sm` for the meaning of the values.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: entropy_source
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Configuration and status registers for the entropy source

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: COMPONENT_ID
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Component Identification

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: NAME
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Entropy Source

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MINOR_VERSION
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Minor Version

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Major Version

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CTRL
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Entropy Source Control

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RESET
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Software controlled reset when asserted high. Resets all internal state including health test counters, FIFO pointers, decorrelator shift registers, and the downsample phase counter. Ring oscillators continue running. Level-sensitive: the reset holds while this bit is 1, so software must write 0 to release it.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MODULE_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Master enable for the OpenTitan entropy_src_main_sm boot/startup gate. Drives main_sm's enable_i. When 0, main_sm stays in Idle and MAIN_SM_STATUS.BOOT_PHASE_DONE never asserts, so no entropy reaches the whitener/FIFO. When 1 (default), main_sm runs the boot health-test window and asserts BOOT_PHASE_DONE once it passes. Locked by FIPS_LOCK.LOCK. See doc/main_sm_boot_gate_functional_compat.md.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTOTUNE_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable automatic detuning of individual ring oscillator noise generators when corresponding per-generator health tests fail. When enabled, a failing health test causes the generator's noise RO to switch to its detuned (higher frequency) tap point. The shared sampling RO also detunes if ANY generator requests it. Automatic detuning is disabled by default (manual tuning via RING_OSC_TUNE required). Locked by FIPS_LOCK.LOCK: the lock freezes this field at whatever value it holds when FIPS_LOCK is set (swwel is value-agnostic). The certified flow writes 0 and then locks, so the entropy-source noise geometry cannot silently self-adjust mid-operation (SP 800-90B validated configuration).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BYPASS_ENTROPY_COMPRESSOR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Bypass Entropy Compressor (BIW extractor) when asserted high. When bypassed, all 96 bytes from the 12 generators (8 bytes each) are pushed directly into the FIFO without compression, increasing FIFO fill rate by 3x (96 bytes vs 32 bits per cycle). Used for raw entropy analysis and testing. Disabled by default (32-bit compressed output). Locked by FIPS_LOCK.LOCK: raw (uncompressed, unconditioned) output is not a validated FIPS mode, so firmware locks this at 0 for certified operation.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DOWNSAMPLE_RATE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Downsample Rate for the decorrelator output. Specifies additional clock cycles to wait between entropy byte outputs. Value of N means output every (N+1) cycles. Applied after DECORRELATOR_CTRL.SAMPLE_CLK_DIV. Example: if SAMPLE_CLK_DIV=63 (div64) and DOWNSAMPLE_RATE=3, effective rate is div256 (64*(3+1)). Default=0 (no additional downsampling). Locked by FIPS_LOCK.LOCK (only wired into the push path in BYPASS_ENTROPY_COMPRESSOR mode).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SHA256_WHITENING_ENABLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable SHA-256 whitening stage after BIW compression. When enabled, 16 × 32-bit BIW outputs (512 bits) are accumulated and hashed using SHA-256, producing 8 × 32-bit digest words (256 bits). This provides cryptographic conditioning per NIST SP 800-90B. When disabled, BIW output goes directly to FIFO (passthrough mode). Default=1 (enabled). Locked by FIPS_LOCK.LOCK: the vetted conditioning component must not be disabled during certified operation.

ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Entropy Source Status (currently unused, reserved for future expansion)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RSVD
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reserved for future use. Always reads 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: DEBUG_CTRL
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Debug control to monitor internal entropy noise source signals.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SELECT_SIGNAL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Select Signal. Selects one of 256 internal signals to route to the external debug monitor pin. Signal mapping: [0-11]: Raw noise bits from generators 0-11 (1 bit per generator). [12-15]: Reserved. [16-27]: Divided sample clocks from generators 0-11 (1 bit per generator). [28-31]: Reserved. [32-63]: Compressed 32-bit entropy stream (BIW extractor output). [64-95]: FIFO input 32-bit entropy stream (pre-FIFO buffering). [96-127]: Reserved. [128-223]: Uncompressed per-generator entropy bytes (96 bits total): Generator 0 byte [135:128], Generator 1 byte [143:136], Generator 2 byte [151:144], Generator 3 byte [159:152], Generator 4 byte [167:160], Generator 5 byte [175:168], Generator 6 byte [183:176], Generator 7 byte [191:184], Generator 8 byte [199:192], Generator 9 byte [207:200], Generator 10 byte [215:208], Generator 11 byte [223:216]. [224-255]: Reserved. Reserved selections drive the signal mux output to 0. With SELECT_FREQ_DIV=0 the external monitor pin is also 0. With SELECT_FREQ_DIV nonzero, the selected ripple-divider stage retains its previous value while the mux output is 0, so the monitor pin can hold 0 or 1 until the divider is reset. Set SELECT_FREQ_DIV=0 before selecting a reserved value when a constant-zero pin output is required.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SELECT_FREQ_DIV
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Select Frequency Divider for debug monitor output pin. Division ratios: 0=div1 (no division), 1=div2, 2=div4, 3=div8, 4=div16, 5=div32, 6=div64, 7=div128. Used to slow down high-frequency signals for external observation. Default=0 (no division).

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: INTR_STATUS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Interrupt Status (write 1 to clear)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HEALTH_TEST_FAILED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Health Test Failed Interrupt. Set when any enabled health test (Repetition, APT, or Markov) fails on the 32-bit entropy stream or any per-generator test fails. Check HEALTH_TEST_STATUS and GENERATOR_*_HEALTH_STATUS for details. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_ERROR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Error Interrupt. Set on FIFO read/write protocol violations. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Overflow Interrupt. Set when entropy data is pushed to a full FIFO (64 entries deep). Data is discarded on overflow. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_UNDERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Underflow Interrupt. Set when software reads from an empty FIFO. Read returns stale/undefined data. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PERSISTENT_FAILURE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Persistent Failure Interrupt. Set when the health-test alert threshold is reached (ALERT_SUMMARY_FAIL_COUNTS.ANY_FAIL_COUNT >= ALERT_THRESHOLD), asserting main_sm.alert_thresh_fail_i and latching MAIN_SM_STATUS.ALERT. Indicates a persistent (not transient) entropy failure requiring firmware attention. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTOTUNE_FAIL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Autotune Failure Interrupt. Set when automatic ring-oscillator detuning fires in response to a per-generator health-test failure (CTRL.AUTOTUNE_ENABLE=1). Signals that the noise-source geometry self-adjusted, which is not permitted during FIPS-certified operation. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BIW_OBS_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: BIW Observe FIFO Overflow Interrupt. Set when a word is pushed to the full post-BIW diagnostic observe FIFO (BIW_OBS); the word is dropped. A gap in the diagnostic mirror is benign, but indicates software is not draining BIW_OBS_RDATA fast enough. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: NOISE_OBS_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Noise Observe FIFO Overflow Interrupt. Set when a word is pushed to the full raw per-lane observe FIFO (NOISE_OBS); the word is dropped. This is a gap in the SP 800-90B raw-noise collection run for the selected lane, so software should drain NOISE_OBS_RDATA before the FIFO fills. Write 1 to clear.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: INTR_ENABLE
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Interrupt Enable (individual enable bits for each interrupt source)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HEALTH_TEST_FAILED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Health Test Failed Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on health test failures. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_ERROR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Error Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on FIFO errors. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Overflow Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on FIFO overflow. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_UNDERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Underflow Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on FIFO underflow. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PERSISTENT_FAILURE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Persistent Failure Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on persistent health-test failure. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: AUTOTUNE_FAIL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Autotune Failure Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation on automatic detune events. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BIW_OBS_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: BIW Observe FIFO Overflow Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation when the post-BIW diagnostic observe FIFO overflows. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: NOISE_OBS_OVERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Noise Observe FIFO Overflow Interrupt Enable. Set to 1 to enable interrupt generation when the raw per-lane observe FIFO overflows. Default=0 (disabled).

ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Interrupt Test (write 1 to manually trigger interrupt for testing)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HEALTH_TEST_FAILED

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_ERROR

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_OVERFLOW

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FIFO_UNDERFLOW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: FIFO Underflow Interrupt Test. Write 1 to manually set INTR_STATUS.FIFO_UNDERFLOW for interrupt handler testing. Self-clearing.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PERSISTENT_FAILURE
